question: What is the primary goal of aseptic technique in nursing practice?

options.B: Eliminating the need for hand washing
options.C: Reducing the cost of hospital supplies

explanation: Asepsis aims to stop harmful microorganisms from entering clean or sterile body sites, thereby preventing infection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h1)

question: Surgical asepsis differs from medical asepsis because surgical asepsis aims to do what?

options.A: Eliminate all microorganisms and spores completely
options.B: Target viral pathogens while ignoring bacteria
options.C: Apply only to non-invasive bedside nursing care
options.D: Reduce only the number of visible dirt particles

explanation: While medical asepsis reduces the number of germs, surgical asepsis removes every living microbe and spore from an item or field. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h1)

question: Administering a routine oral medication to a ward patient primarily relies on which practice?
explanation: Routine non-invasive care uses medical asepsis to keep pathogen numbers low and stop cross-infection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h2)

question: Inserting an indwelling urinary catheter requires the nurse to utilize which technique?
explanation: The urinary bladder is normally sterile, so entering it requires surgical asepsis to prevent introducing pathogens. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h2)

question: A contaminated surgical instrument acts as which link in the chain of infection?
explanation: An unsterilized instrument transfers pathogens directly from one environment or person to another. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h3)

question: How does thorough hand washing primarily help stop the chain of infection?

options.A: By interrupting the mode of transmission
options.B: By closing the portal of entry permanently
options.C: By eliminating the susceptible host completely
options.D: By destroying the infectious agent inside the body

explanation: Washing hands removes transient microbes, preventing them from being carried from surfaces or patients to others. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the single most effective method for preventing the spread of infections in clinical settings?
explanation: Frequent and correct hand cleaning removes transient microorganisms before they can cause infection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h4)

question: When must a nurse choose soap and water over an alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: When entering a general medical ward
options.B: When hands are visibly soiled with organic material
options.C: Before performing a sterile dressing change

explanation: Alcohol rubs do not remove physical dirt, blood, or body fluids effectively, requiring soap and water washing. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which item of personal protective equipment should be removed first during the doffing process?
explanation: Gloves are usually the most contaminated items and are removed first to prevent touching other clean body areas or PPE. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why is the correct sequence for removing personal protective equipment strictly enforced?

options.A: To comply with hospital fashion and dress codes
options.B: To speed up the process of leaving an isolation room
options.C: To minimize the risk of self-contamination during removal
options.D: To ensure equipment can be washed and reused safely

explanation: Following a set doffing order stops pathogens on dirty gear from transferring to skin or clean clothes. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h5)

question: An item dropped below which physical landmark is immediately considered contaminated?
explanation: Items kept below waist level are out of the immediate visual field and are treated as unsterile. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why is a sterile drape touching a wet table surface considered contaminated?

options.A: Wet tables generate excessive heat that destroys sterile items
options.B: Moisture changes the color of the sterile fabric immediately
options.C: Wet surfaces automatically dissolve the chemical sterilization on drapes
options.D: Moisture allows bacteria to cross the barrier via capillary action

explanation: Liquid acts as a wick, drawing microorganisms from unsterile surfaces through the drape into the sterile zone. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of disposing of used needles immediately into a safety box?

options.A: Ensuring needles are securely locked away for laboratory testing
options.B: Preventing accidental needle-stick injuries and bloodborne infections
options.C: Making it easier to count how many injections were given
options.D: Reducing the overall financial cost of hospital waste disposal

explanation: Puncture-resistant containers protect staff and patients from injuries that spread viruses like HIV and hepatitis. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h7)

question: When municipal water supply to a ward is interrupted, what is the best immediate infection control practice?

options.A: Wiping hands with a common cloth towel instead
options.B: Using alcohol-based hand rubs for routine hand cleansing
options.C: Skipping hand hygiene to save time during emergencies
options.D: Postponing all patient care tasks until water returns

explanation: Alcohol hand rubs serve as an effective alternative for cleaning non-soiled hands during water shortages. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h7)
